description.narrative: Avslutande stöd till Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS) för programmet ”Stärkt Forskning, Utbildning och Innovation för Hållbar Utveckling” under åren 2024-2030. Programmets övergripande mål är att konsolidera samt stärka forskningskapaciteten vid MUHAS för att bidra till hållbar kapacitet att bedriva forskning som är relevant hälsoforskning för fattigdomsbekämpning och socialt, ekonomiskt och miljömässigt hållbar utveckling. Programmet innehåller fem delprogram, varav fyra forskarutbildningsprogram inom olika relevanta forskningsområden inom hälsa relaterade till Tanzanias utveckling (malaria och tuberkulos, HIV/Aids, mödra- och barnhälsa, samt hälsosystem) och ett forskningsstödjandeprogram (forskningsadministration, forskningskommunikation, kvalitetssäkring av forskarutbildning och innovationssystem och immaterialrätt). Programmet kommer att implementeras av MUHAS i partnerskap med fyra svenska universitet. MUHAS har lokal ackrediterade doktorandprogram som har utvecklats tillsammans med svenska partners och MUHAS bedöms ha tillräcklig egen handledningskapacitet inom dessa områden.

Final support to Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS) for the programme ‘Strengthening Research, Training and Innovation for Sustainable Development’ for the years 2024-2030. The overall objective of the programme is to consolidate and strengthen research capacity at MUHAS to contribute to sustainable capacity to conduct research that is relevant to health research for poverty reduction and socially, economically and environmentally sustainable development. The programme comprises five sub-programmes, including four postgraduate programmes in different relevant health research areas related to Tanzania's development (malaria and tuberculosis, HIV/AIDS, maternal and child health, and health systems) and one research support programme (research administration, research communication, quality assurance of postgraduate education and innovation systems, and intellectual property). The programme will be implemented by MUHAS in partnership with four Swedish universities. MUHAS has locally accredited PhD programmes developed together with Swedish partners and MUHAS is deemed to have sufficient in-house supervision capacity in these areas.

title.narrative: Grant agreement between Sweden and Tanzania regarding Strengtherning research,training and innovation for sustainable development

description.narrative:
The programme started in 2025.
All 16 PhD candidates have been recruited. An advert communicating the MUHAS-Sida scholarship was disseminated within and outside MUHAS (15th Jan to 15th Feb 2025). A transparent selection process utilizing University mechanisms was employed to competitively award the scholarships.
A total of 153 complete applications were received by the 15th of February 2025 deadline, and submitted to the sub programs.
The selection process was structured around four distinct subprograms: The Reproductive and Child Health subprogram received 50 applications Malaria and NTDS had 28 applications HIV/TB attracted 34 applications Health Systems Research garnered 41 applications.
Each subprogram employed standardized evaluation tool, adapted with context-specific criteria to conduct an internal review, shortlisting, and subsequent candidate interviews (using both virtual and physical formats) to ensure consistency and fairness.
There are four continuing PhD students, one female and one male from RCH Subprogram and two female from HIV/TB subprogram.
